summary: The Michael Enzi Voluntary Protection Program Act of 2025 gives statutory authority to the Voluntary Protection Programs within the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). It sets official requirements for employers who volunteer to create comprehensive safety and health management systems, exempts participating worksites from OSHA-initiated programmed inspections, prohibits any fees for participation, directs the modernization of program technology, and mandates that at least 5 percent of OSHA's annual appropriated funds be dedicated to the program.

affected_groups.effect: Volunteering employers can apply to participate, must meet safety management requirements, conduct self-evaluations, allow onsite evaluations, and are exempt from programmed OSHA inspections without paying any qualification or participation fees.
Benefit from worksites implementing systematic hazard assessments, safety training, management and employee participation, and having safety program information readily available.

Required to establish, oversee, monitor, and transition the program, develop a technology modernization plan, issue final regulations within two years, and dedicate at least 5 percent of annual appropriations to fund it.

key_provisions: Establishes the Michael Enzi Voluntary Protection Program within the Department of Labor to recognize employers with comprehensive safety and health management systems.

Requires participating employers to submit applications, conduct annual self-evaluations, undergo onsite evaluations by OSHA representatives, and correct identified serious hazards or violations within 90 days or as soon as practicable.
Exempts approved worksites from programmed inspections by OSHA during their participation in the program.
Prohibits the Department of Labor from charging any form of payment for employers to qualify for or participate in the program or the basic tiered challenge program.
Requires the Secretary of Labor to create a written plan within two years to modernize the technology used for program applications, self-evaluations, and audit reporting.
Mandates that the Secretary of Labor use at least 5 percent of OSHA's annual appropriated funds to carry out the act.
missing_information: Specific total dollar amounts of OSHA's annual appropriations that will constitute the 5 percent funding floor.
Exact details or criteria of the final regulations that the Secretary of Labor is required to issue within two years.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Michael Enzi Voluntary Protection Program Act of 2025 gives statutory authority to the Voluntary Protection Programs within the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). It sets official requirements for employers who volunteer to create comprehensive safety and health management systems, exempts participating worksites from OSHA-initiated programmed inspections, prohibits any fees for participation, directs the modernization of program technology, and mandates that at least 5 percent of OSHA's annual appropriated funds be dedicated to the program.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes formal statutory backing for an existing OSHA cooperative initiative, setting specific oversight, funding requirements of at least 5 percent of OSHA appropriations, technology modernization mandates, and inspection exemptions for participating worksites.
